issues.description: Ties are the cause, but the draft's breakdown of the mechanism puts the weight on the wrong part. Without ties, the planted order gives the minimum possible sum, because the code's chain is a Prim tree and the nearest strictly earlier members then form the MST. In simulation, breaking ties along the chain gives z = -18 to -21. The main driver is the large tie at the last checkpoint. The branch order fills it with the pole's WordNet outliers (within-pole nearest-neighbour distance 7.5 to 8.3, against 5.1 to 5.6 for all classes). Classes tied there do not count as earlier for one another, so each outlier is measured to the core. Breaking only the last-checkpoint ties reverses the sign (z +4.2..+6.3 becomes -2.6..-5.8). The exclusion the draft names first ('only classes with an earlier member are counted', which under a branch order drops the core at the first checkpoint) is the smaller part: breaking only the first-checkpoint ties lowers z by 1.1 to 2.4 but leaves it positive.

The draft's own tercile null shows that some strength-linked WordNet structure exists that the |log R| Mantel misses: the late-block tercile null mean is 0.0060, about 33 standard errors above 0 and above the plain null (-0.0001), while the |log R| Mantel is 0.001. That model reproduces every late-block number. So the reported controls cannot tell WordNet-driven co-entry from a pure strength route. The model needs atypical draws (about 5% accepted; without the selection its |log R| Mantel is 0.41), so this route is possible but not likely. It has not been ruled out.

issues.description: T4 does not orient the writes by the sign of the net value. It uses W_k with its stored sign (pos = clip(W, 0)) for every final pole class, including classes whose net value vbar_c is negative. For those classes the unit's positive response runs through a negative gate and a negative value, so the writes that build the response are the negative ones. The 'positive mass' then measures writes that work against the value, and a high own percentile means the class's own writes push against it. In stages 0 and 1 these classes are a large part of the population, so the early-block own and relative shares and percentiles mix two opposite orientations. The reading 'no larger than a typical class' in stages 0 and 1 is therefore not established. convnext_growth.py skips vbar <= 0 for exactly this reason ('the gate opened it with a negative value'); the test code dropped that guard.

T1, first bullet (replace from 'has no power' to the end of the bullet): With WordNet distance and these tied entry checkpoints, the nearest-earlier statistic of the first analysis is not a valid test of branch order. A planted growth order raises it, z = +7 to +13 in every block, which is the opposite of the direction the first analysis tested. The planted order reassigns the observed entry checkpoints along a greedy growth from the strongest class, each step adding the class nearest to any class already added. The cause is ties: only classes with an earlier member are counted, and the planted order gives the earliest tied checkpoints to the core of the pole and the latest to its WordNet outliers. The observed statistic is also above its null (pooled z = +5.0; +4.2 against the tercile null), in the planted direction. The first analysis's other statistic, the share of entering classes with an earlier relative, does not rise under a planted order either, and is below its null (pooled z = -3.8). Both readings in the bullet 'Order of growth (E2) is not shown' above are withdrawn. With visual distance (DINOv2 neighbour ranks, growth_tests_visual.json.gz) the planted order lowers the nearest-earlier statistic (z = -1.6 to -7.5), and the observed one is below its null as well (pooled z = -6.2; -3.5 against the tercile null). The sign of this statistic therefore depends on the distance.

T2, last sentence: Over the full range of distances (about 10 steps) this is 0.04 of a checkpoint interval. The slope is detectable when blocks are pooled with equal weights (z = 3.2; 2.5 with inverse-variance weights, and 1.65 for the late blocks) and negligible in size. Two departures from the planned test: the anchor is the unit's strongest final class, not its first classes, and there is no planted outward order to show what slope the test would detect.

T2, block count: 3 of 18 blocks p <= 0.003, 5 of 18 p <= 0.04.

T3, mean lag and reading: Mean lag at 50%: -0.07 to 0.40 checkpoint (relatives first in 16 of 18 blocks; bootstrap interval over units excludes 0 in 12 of 18). T3 has no null. A difference in noise level between one class's part and a sum of about 10 parts gives the same pattern without any head start: in a simulation with this run's checkpoints and learning-rate schedule, mean lag is +0.3 to +0.7 checkpoint, median 0, relatives first 47 to 53%. With visual relatives, which write more into the class, the lead is smaller (pooled 0.08 against 0.18 checkpoint; the interval excludes 0 in 2 of 18 blocks). The parts are also evaluated at each checkpoint's own input and strongest position, so their trajectories mix accumulated writes with upstream drift. The lag is not evidence for a head start until it is compared with the lag between the own part and as many random groups (run E1r).

T4, own share: Positive mass, median over pole classes: own 0.000 to 0.004 (the chance median for a random class is about 0, and the chance mean is 0.001). The own part's percentile among the 999 other classes' parts is 0.52 to 0.59 in 5 of 6 early blocks (0.40 in stage1.block2). In stage 2 it is 0.51 to 0.82, rising toward stage 3, and in stage 3 it is 0.83 to 0.92.

T5, early blocks and relatives: Late blocks: entering classes survive more often, by +0.02 to +0.09 in 10 of 12 blocks. Early blocks: less often in 4 of 6 (more often in stage0.block0 and stage0.block1). This survival is close to the share of classes whose own value part is negative (correlation 0.93 over blocks and groups), so the own knockout is mostly a sign test of the own part. Without all relatives' writes, entering classes survive more often than incumbents in 10 of 12 late blocks, by +0.01 to +0.04. A head start carried by relatives predicts less often. Margin does not explain either difference: without the writes of as many random classes, entering classes survive slightly less often (late, pooled -0.01).

Result for E2 and E3 on this run, with WordNet distance. Late-block units are coherent groups of related classes (Sec. above). WordNet relatives enter a unit at slightly more similar times than chance (T1: late blocks r = 0.029 against 0.006 for the strength-matched null, about 6% of a planted growth from the strongest class). This is co-timing, not order. A class clock shared by relatives, where related classes become separable at the same time anywhere in the network, would give it too, and that has not been controlled.

The half-rise of a class's response moves outward from the unit's strongest class by 0.0035 checkpoint per WordNet step (T2). This is detectable when pooled and negligible in size. The relatives' part reaches half its final value a fraction of a checkpoint before the own part (T3), but without a null, and a noise-level difference alone gives the same pattern.

At entry, in 11 of 12 late blocks most classes would leave the pole without their own writes: survival is 0.26 to 0.53, against 0.51 to 0.58 without the writes of 10 random classes. Entering classes survive this knockout slightly more often than incumbents, the direction a head start predicts, mainly because their own value part is more often negative. They do not depend more on their relatives' writes than incumbents do (T5).

Each pole class's value is a small remainder of large cancelling writes (T4: summed absolute parts are 300 to 575 times the net value). Removing 10 random classes' writes moves 40 to 56% of pole classes across the threshold. How much of each part is class structure, and how much is noise, needs the random-group split. Neither recursive growth nor a head start shows at the size the essay describes; small effects remain that need the controls below.

The essay authors' own early-training notes are similarly cautious on a different test. Zeroing a candidate broad-car precursor unit moved the final ambulance unit by amounts 'within the range of matched controls', and they write that their trajectories 'do not yet demonstrate a causal generalist-to-specialist consolidation mechanism'. Their test asks whether a specialist unit inherits from a generalist unit; ours asks in what order, and from whose writes, classes join one unit. The two agree in caution, not in a matched result.

So does pooling over checkpoints: incumbents are counted once per later entry event, so they are weighted toward later checkpoints, and no stratification is done. (b) Being near the threshold pushes entering classes' survival DOWN under the one-sided own and relatives knockouts. T5, knockout at entry. With class means of gate and value at each probe image's strongest position, R'_c = SiLU(G_c - G_c,own) (V_c - V_c,own). This removes the class's writes into this unit's gate and value maps only; the block input, which the same class also wrote through earlier blocks, and the strongest positions are held fixed. A class 'survives' if R'_c is at least the 20th strongest approximate response among the other classes. The bar is held fixed: the other classes' responses are not recomputed after the knockout, although removing a class's or its relatives' writes also lowers them, and the relatives are often pole members. The approximation (product of class means) puts 62 to 81% of entering classes and 73 to 91% of incumbents above the bar without any knockout (100% if it were exact). Rates below are conditional on that. 'Entering' means the stable-entry checkpoint; checkpoints are up to 5,000 steps apart, and every class writes into every unit from the first step. Survival without own writes: entering 0.26 to 0.65, incumbents at the same checkpoint 0.17 to 0.70. In the late blocks (stages 2 and 3), entering classes survive more often in 10 of 12 blocks (by +0.02 to +0.09; pooled 0.36 against 0.32). They survive less often in stage 1 and in stage-0 block 2 (by 0.04 to 0.09), and slightly more often in stage-0 blocks 0 and 1 (+0.03, +0.02). Without all relatives' writes: entering classes survive more often than incumbents in 10 of 12 late blocks (by +0.01 to +0.04; -0.01 and -0.02 in stage-2 blocks 0 and 3). Pooled, the difference is +0.02, and +0.01 without the conditioning. They survive less often in 5 of 6 early blocks. Without the writes of as many random non-relative classes as the class has relatives (median 10, 2 to 35 for 80% of classes; 5% of classes have none and then survive both group knockouts trivially): survival 0.44 to 0.60 in both groups, entering slightly lower in 9 of 12 late blocks (pooled 0.55 against 0.56).
- Reading: In late blocks, removing a class's own writes, or its relatives' writes, puts more pole classes below the bar than removing the writes of as many random classes (one exception: incumbents in stage-2 block 3). Own and relatives' writes push the class up consistently, while random writes push it either way. That is class structure. At its stable entry, a late-block entering class falls below the bar without its own writes in 64% of cases, against 45% without random classes. At this checkpoint resolution, its own writes already carry most entering classes when they join, so a strict head start (firing before the class writes) is not seen. Entering classes lose less than incumbents from both their own and their relatives' knockout, although they sit closer to the bar (lower calibration, slightly lower survival under the random knockout), which by itself would lower their survival. Any account in which a class's own and relatives' writes keep growing after it joins predicts this. A head start carried by relatives predicts the reverse for the relatives' knockout, and that is not seen. The relatives' difference is small and about the size of the bias from the fixed bar (in a toy with cancelling parts, recomputing the bar over the pole classes changed it by -0.01 to -0.02). So the data show no head start carried by relatives, and they do not show the opposite either.
